newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Equipment firm Kian Ann may issue 30 mln shares.
newsitem.headline: Equipment firm Kian Ann may issue 30 mln shares.

text.p: Heavy equipment and spare-part supplier Kian Ann Engineering is expected to offer about 30 million shares in its initial public offering next week, dealers said on Thursday.
Dealers said the offer price was likely to be around Singapore 60 cents per share.
Kian Ann's general manager, Chew Thiam Keng, told Reuters: "We are targeting the IPO for sometime next week."
He said the company was completing details of the proposed offering with its lead manager, Development Bank of Singapore (DBS).
A DBS source confirmed Kian Ann has received approval in principle from the Stock Exchange of Singapore for a main-board listing.

Brokers said about six million shares, less than originally intended, would be placed out at S$0.60 each. They said the strong performance of recent IPOs have encouraged Kian Ann to offer more shares to the public.
About half of the placement shares have been taken up, they said.
Chew said all proceeds from the offer "would be used to tap opportunities in Southeast Asia (SEA) infrastructure projects".
"This (infrastructure) market is really taking off. It will propel the economies of SEA and we are in perfect position to take advantage of this," Chew said.
The company supplies more than half a million types of spare parts for heavy industrial equipment like bulldozers and tractors used in construction, logging, mining and infrastructure development.
Chew said more than 60 percent of Kian Ann's revenue comes from overseas sales. Malaysia, Indonesia, Brunei, Myanmar, Thailand, India, Pakistan and Hong Kong are some of its markets.
For the fiscal year ended June 30, 1996, Kian Ann recorded a pretax profit of S$7 million on a turnover of S$60 million.
Kian Ann's closest competitors are Malaysia Triumphal Associates and Singapore Hoe Leong Corporation.
Some analysts felt the offering would be well-received as its pricing made for a historic price earnings (PE) ratio of 10.80 times, which they considered attractive.
"The fundamentals are also good since about 60 percent of the company's sales are generated from overseas customers," one analyst said.
